issues.what: Magic rule stated as pencil-only and 'from your own hands', but Farzana flies strangers' griefs and later chapters write in marker and lipstick
issues.quote: Write it on the paper in pencil, fly it from your own hands at Basant

issues.what: Neighbours fly home-made shopping-bag kites, yet the magic belongs to Qureshi kites; muddles the rule at the climax
issues.quote: with a pink kite made from a shopping bag

issues.what: Ninety-seven kites carried up 'two nights' - but ch2 is the first night and she was only 'checking the back room'
issues.quote: Farzana had spent two nights carrying them up in vegetable bags after isha.

issues.what: Kite count skips the intervening nights and Tariq's superior is oddly also 'Bhatti sahib'
issues.quote: Bhatti sahib upstairs says extra patrol tomorrow.

issues.what: Zubaida's shawl is white here, black everywhere else (and in the brief)
issues.quote: stuck out from under a white shawl

issues.what: Typo 'chaps' for chappals; repeated wrist-slap and 'fingers remembered' beats from ch2
issues.quote: Farzana felt her stomach drop to her chaps.

issues.what: Phrase 'knee deep where Zubaida had swept all winter' repeated in ch3, ch4 and ch5; 'light as paper', pressure-cooker/dog-barked beats repeated; 'three' kites listed as two
issues.quote: Against the far parapet it stood knee deep where Zubaida had swept all winter

fix: Ch1: restate rule without pencil/own-hands and fix shawl colour. Ch3: first-evening carry, typo, trim repeated beats. Ch4: kite count across nights, SHO not Bhatti, trim repeats. Ch5: neighbours fly Qureshi kites from the stack, fix count, trim repeated phrases.
praise: Tariq's name on the kite he cannot cut in ch4, paid off in one clean motion at Basant, is genuinely moving.

issues.what: Corbeau's 'last wine of a dead vineyard' scene is repeated as if new, with a contradicting backstory (Clos Roux/laundries vs brother's vineyard/salt pans); ch5 cites the ch4 version
Valley is 'two days inland by mail cart' but she rides there overnight and back overnight; the five-day clock depends on it
issues.quote: Two days inland by mail cart

issues.what: Deed thread never resolved - did her mother sell the spring?
issues.quote: Signed or half signed, she did not know.

issues.what: Badge both in her pocket and put back on; 'a week ago' and 'supper had passed' timeline slips
issues.quote: then put it back on in the dark outside the doors

issues.what: Day count drifts (forty after forty-one); forged slip oddly copies Lemaire's hook
issues.quote: Forty days of it in different inks, same hand.

issues.what: Repeated phrases: 'the sour tang of' ink/chalk, Lemaire 'tall and pale in his blue coat, the silver drop winking', 'knew that hand in her teeth', bicycle bells; Lot 9 was wind, not rain
issues.quote: You stare at Lot 14 the way I stared at Lot 9.

issues.what: Train ticket in a mail-cart world; she bid against the signature 'in spring' though it began forty days ago
issues.quote: She had tried twice in spring

fix: Ch1: travel time, cart fare, 'last month'. Ch2: Lot 9, repeated phrases. Ch3: count, forged slip, repeats. Ch4: cut the second dead-wine tasting, keep the warehouse briefing. Ch5: Corbeau cites Clos Roux, badge/timeline fixes, telegram resolving the deed.
praise: The hail set piece - two opposite bindings on one valley and the sky 'refusing the riddle' - makes the magic's cost vivid and funny.

issues.what: The dog is under Barnaby's arm as he climbs the roof in ch1, but is inside the house behind a window all of ch2
issues.quote: From inside, the mayor’s small nervous dog pressed its nose to the pane

issues.what: Mrs. Pottle's cat lie drifts: cat died, six stone (ch1) vs cat adopted by the blacksmith, two ounces, item one (ch2)
issues.quote: Mrs. Pottle’s cat will pull through.” It didn’t. Six stone

issues.what: Tuppence is 14 but her notebook weighs lies from twenty years ago with no explanation
issues.quote: Every time he came home heavy, I made him step on the kitchen scales.

issues.what: Ch2 restarts the reading ch1 already began (opens notebook, clears throat again); 'windowsills vanishing again, then the sills' glitch; generic title
issues.quote: windowsills vanishing again, then the sills, then the lower panes

fix: Ch1: align the Pottle cat lie with ch2, explain the early entries, put the dog inside through the attic window. Ch2: continue the reading rather than restart it, attic window, fix the sills sentence, retitle.
praise: Barnaby chalking EXCEPT I FAILED ONCE under his own first lie is a funny, kind, exactly earned climax.
